screenplay.text:
LOST PROPERTY

                                     Written by

                                 The Panelwise team






























               Self-written sample screenplay for Panelwise.
               Licence: Apache-2.0, the same as the repository.













               FADE IN:

               EXT. PARK STATION - NIGHT

               Rain sheets down on a grand old railway station. Its clock
               tower reads ten to eleven. A last taxi pulls away, wipers
               beating.

               Under the arches, a hand-painted sign: LOST PROPERTY -
               PLATFORM 9.

               INT. LOST PROPERTY OFFICE - NIGHT

               A long narrow room lined floor to ceiling with shelves.
               Umbrellas in a barrel. A tin bath full of single shoes. A
               rocking horse with one ear. Somewhere, a clock ticks.

               ZANELE (30s), cardigan over her railway uniform, sits behind
               a wooden counter writing in a fat green LEDGER. Beside her
               elbow, a brass BELL.

               A ginger cat, MARMALADE, sleeps on a pile of lost scarves.

               MR. DUBE (60s), the station master, waistcoat and pocket
               watch, backs through the door carrying a box tied with
               string.

                                     MR. DUBE
                         Forty-one years, Zanele. Forty-one
                         years I have walked these
                         platforms, and tonight is my last
                         night shift.

                                     ZANELE
                         You say that as if you're sad about
                         it.

                                     MR. DUBE
                               (setting the box down)
                         I am sad about it. Who will wind
                         the tower clock? Who will chase the
                         pigeons out of the waiting room?

                                     ZANELE
                         Me, probably.

               He peers at the ledger over his spectacles.

                                     MR. DUBE
                         What came in today?












                                                                       2.


                                     ZANELE
                               (reading)
                         Three umbrellas. One wedding hat. A
                         set of false teeth, which I have
                         put in a jar. And a birthday cake,
                         uneaten.

                                     MR. DUBE
                         Whose birthday?

                                     ZANELE
                         It didn't say.

               INT. STATION CONCOURSE - CONTINUOUS

               A vast hall of marble and iron. Almost empty. A SLEEPING
               COMMUTER lies across a bench under a newspaper.

               PRIYA (20), soaked through, a music satchel over one
               shoulder, runs across the concourse, looking everywhere at
               once.

                                     ANNOUNCER (V.O.)
                         The last train to Pretoria has now
                         departed from platform four. There
                         are no further departures tonight.

               Priya stops dead under the departures board. Every line
               reads CANCELLED or DEPARTED.

                                     PRIYA
                               (under her breath)
                         No. No, no, no.

               She spots the hand-painted sign for Lost Property and runs.

               INT. LOST PROPERTY OFFICE - MOMENTS LATER

               The door flies open. The brass bell on the counter jumps.
               Marmalade opens one eye.

                                     PRIYA
                         My violin. I left my violin on the
                         train from Soweto. A black case
                         with a red ribbon on the handle.
                         Please tell me somebody handed it
                         in.

                                     ZANELE
                               (opening the ledger)
                         Which train?











                                                                       3.


                                     PRIYA
                         The nine-fifteen. I fell asleep.
                         When I woke up I was at the end of
                         the line and the case was gone.

               Zanele runs her finger down the page, slowly.

                                     ZANELE
                         Umbrella. Umbrella. Hat. Teeth.
                         Cake. I'm sorry. No violin.

                                     PRIYA
                         It has to be here. My audition is
                         at eight tomorrow morning. It was
                         my grandfather's violin. There is
                         no other one.

               Mr. Dube takes off his cap.

                                     MR. DUBE
                         Sit down, young lady. Nothing is
                         lost at Park Station until I say
                         so.

               He lifts the brass bell and rings it, twice. Loud.

               INT. PLATFORM NINE - NIGHT

               A long covered platform, lit by humming lamps. Rain drums on
               the iron roof.

               KOOS (70s), the night cleaner, pushes a wide broom along the
               platform edge. He wears headphones over a woolly hat and
               hums to himself.

               At the far end, TEBOGO (20s), a busker in a patched denim
               jacket, plays a VIOLIN. A black case lies open at his feet
               with a few coins in it. A red ribbon is tied to its handle.

               The music is beautiful. Koos stops sweeping to listen.

                                     KOOS
                         That's a sad one.

                                     TEBOGO
                               (still playing)
                         It's a sad instrument. I think it
                         misses somebody.

               Two police officers walk onto the platform: OFFICER MOLOI
               (40s), broad and patient, and OFFICER VAN WYK (20s), new,
               eager, notebook already out.










                                                                       4.


                                     OFFICER VAN WYK
                               (whispering)
                         Sarge. Black case. Red ribbon.

                                     OFFICER MOLOI
                         I have eyes, Van Wyk.

               INT. LOST PROPERTY OFFICE - LATER

               Priya sits on a folding chair with a mug of tea she hasn't
               touched. Mr. Dube is on the office telephone, a heavy black
               thing with a curly cord.

                                     MR. DUBE
                               (into phone)
                         Yes, the nine-fifteen. Yes, a
                         violin. Thank you, Tshepo. You are
                         a good man.

               He hangs up.

               The door opens again. GRACE (30s), a nurse still in her
               scrubs, comes in holding the hand of AMAHLE (8), who is
               wearing pyjamas under a yellow raincoat and has clearly been
               crying.

                                     GRACE
                         I'm sorry to come so late. We lost
                         a giraffe.

                                     ZANELE
                         A giraffe.

                                     AMAHLE
                         A toy one. His name is Gerald. He
                         has a blue scarf and one of his
                         legs is shorter than the others.

                                     ZANELE
                               (gently)
                         When did you last see Gerald?

                                     AMAHLE
                         On the escalator. I was holding him
                         up so he could see the pigeons, and
                         then he wasn't there any more.

               Zanele writes it carefully in the ledger.

                                     ZANELE
                         Giraffe. Gerald. Blue scarf. One
                         short leg.










                                                                       5.


               A knock on the open door. SAM (20s), a bicycle courier in a
               dripping rain cape, holds up a clipboard.

                                     SAM
                         Delivery for a Mr. Dube? I was told
                         to bring it here at eleven exactly.

               Sam hands over a flat white box. Mr. Dube frowns at it.

                                     MR. DUBE
                         I didn't order anything.

                                     SAM
                         It's paid for. Sign here, please.

               He signs. Sam salutes with the clipboard and is gone.

               INT. PLATFORM NINE - CONTINUOUS

               Tebogo finishes the tune and lowers the violin. The two
               officers stand in front of him.

                                     OFFICER MOLOI
                         Evening. That's a fine instrument.

                                     TEBOGO
                         It isn't mine.

                                     OFFICER VAN WYK
                               (scribbling)
                         Suspect admits instrument is not
                         his.

                                     OFFICER MOLOI
                         Van Wyk.

                                     TEBOGO
                         I found it on the nine-fifteen,
                         under a seat. I was going to take
                         it to Lost Property, but the office
                         light was off when I passed, and
                         then it started raining, and then
                         --
                               (beat)
                         I thought if I played it, whoever
                         lost it might hear.

                                     KOOS
                         He's been playing for an hour.
                         Nobody came.

                                     OFFICER MOLOI
                         Somebody might have. Pack it up,
                         son. We're going for a walk.








                                                                       6.


               INT. STATION CONCOURSE - LATER

               Priya stands at the concourse railing with Zanele. The
               sleeping commuter snores under his newspaper.

               Faintly, from far away, violin music echoes off the marble.
               Then it stops.

                                     PRIYA
                         Did you hear that?

                                     ZANELE
                         Hear what?

                                     PRIYA
                         That was my grandfather's tune. I
                         would know it anywhere. Nobody else
                         plays it.

               She is already running toward the platforms.

                                     ZANELE
                         Priya, wait!

               INT. LOST PROPERTY OFFICE - NIGHT

               Officer Moloi steers Tebogo through the door, the violin
               case under his arm. Officer Van Wyk follows. Then Priya, out
               of breath. Then Zanele.

               Everyone is suddenly in the small room at once. Marmalade
               leaves in disgust.

                                     PRIYA
                         That's it. That's my case.

                                     OFFICER VAN WYK
                         We found the suspect playing it on
                         platform nine.

                                     TEBOGO
                         I'm not a suspect. I'm a musician.

                                     OFFICER MOLOI
                         He says he found it on the nine-
                         fifteen.

               Priya opens the case. Inside the lid, a faded photograph of
               an old man holding the same violin.

                                     PRIYA
                               (quietly)
                         It's here. It's all here.









                                                                       7.


               She turns to Tebogo.

                                     PRIYA
                         You played his tune. How do you
                         know his tune?

                                     TEBOGO
                         I didn't. The music was folded in
                         the case. I just read it.

               A long moment. Then Priya laughs, and cries a little, and
               laughs again.

                                     MR. DUBE
                         Officers, I believe this is a case
                         of lost property, and lost property
                         is my department.

                                     OFFICER MOLOI
                               (closing his notebook)
                         Then we'll leave it with you, Mr.
                         Dube.

                                     OFFICER VAN WYK
                         But Sarge, the paperwork --

                                     OFFICER MOLOI
                         Van Wyk.

               The officers leave. Amahle tugs at her mother's scrubs.

                                     AMAHLE
                         Mama, what about Gerald?

               INT. CONCOURSE RAFTERS - NIGHT

               High above the concourse, among iron beams and pigeons, Koos
               climbs a tall wooden LADDER with a torch in his teeth.

               He reaches into a nest of twigs and newspaper and pulls out
               a small toy GIRAFFE in a blue scarf.

               A pigeon glares at him.

                                     KOOS
                         Sorry, my friend. He's already got
                         a home.

               INT. LOST PROPERTY OFFICE - LATER

               Koos comes in with the giraffe held up high like a trophy.

                                     KOOS
                         Is anybody missing a Gerald?








                                                                       8.


               Amahle shrieks and hugs the giraffe so hard his short leg
               sticks straight out.

                                     AMAHLE
                         Gerald! You went to see the pigeons
                         without me!

                                     GRACE
                         Thank you. Thank you, all of you.

               Mr. Dube unties the string on the white box. Inside is a
               cake, iced with the words HAPPY RETIREMENT MR. DUBE - FROM
               PLATFORM 9.

                                     MR. DUBE
                         Who did this?

                                     ZANELE
                               (shrugging)
                         Lost property. Nobody claimed it.

               Mr. Dube looks at the cake for a long moment. He takes out
               his handkerchief and blows his nose, loudly.

                                     MR. DUBE
                         Well. Someone find me a knife. And
                         plates. And Tebogo, if you would
                         play something that isn't sad.

               Tebogo looks at Priya. She hands him the violin.

                                     PRIYA
                         Just one song. Then I need it back.
                         I have somewhere to be at eight.

               Tebogo plays something bright and quick. Amahle dances with
               Gerald. Koos taps his broom. Even Marmalade comes back to
               the doorway to watch.

               EXT. PLATFORM FOUR - DAWN

               The rain has stopped. Pale gold light slides along the
               rails. The first train of the day sighs to a stop.

               Priya steps aboard with the violin case held tight against
               her chest. At the window she waves.

               On the platform, Tebogo raises his hand. Beside him, Mr.
               Dube winds his pocket watch one last time and looks up at
               the station clock.

                                     MR. DUBE
                         Right on time.









                                                                       9.


                                     ANNOUNCER (V.O.)
                         The six-oh-five to Pretoria is now
                         departing from platform four.

               The train pulls away into the morning.

                                                            FADE OUT.

Umbrella. Umbrella. Hat. Teeth. Cake. I'm sorry. No violin.
It has to be here. My audition is at eight tomorrow morning. It was my grandfather's violin. There is no other one.
Mr. Dube takes off his cap.
shots.rationale: Captures the emotional weight of Priya's plea and Mr. Dube's authoritative dismissal.

shots.source:
Sit down, young lady. Nothing is lost at Park Station until I say so.
He lifts the brass bell and rings it, twice. Loud.
shots.rationale: Shows Mr. Dube ringing the bell to signal the end of the search, framing both characters for the resolution.

shots.source:
A long covered platform, lit by humming lamps. Rain drums on the iron roof.
KOOS (70s), the night cleaner, pushes a wide broom along the platform edge. He wears headphones over a woolly hat and hums to himself.
At the far end, TEBOGO (20s), a busker in a patched denim jacket, plays a VIOLIN. A black case lies open at his feet with a few coins in it. A red ribbon is tied to its handle.
shots.rationale: Establishes the night platform and introduces the two main characters and their props before dialogue begins.

shots.source:
The music is beautiful. Koos stops sweeping to listen.
That's a sad one.
It's a sad instrument. I think it misses somebody.
shots.rationale: Captures the reaction shot as Koos stops sweeping and listens to the violin, focusing on the interaction.

shots.source:
Two police officers walk onto the platform: OFFICER MOLOI (40s), broad and patient, and OFFICER VAN WYK (20s), new, eager, notebook already out.
Sarge. Black case. Red ribbon.
I have eyes, Van Wyk.
shots.rationale: Follows the officers onto the platform, matching their hushed conversation about the violin case.

shots.source:
Priya sits on a folding chair with a mug of tea she hasn't touched. Mr. Dube is on the office telephone, a heavy black thing with a curly cord.
Yes, the nine-fifteen. Yes, a violin. Thank you, Tshepo. You are a good man.
He hangs up.
shots.rationale: Establishes Priya's presence and Mr. Dube's phone call before he hangs up.

shots.source:
The door opens again. GRACE (30s), a nurse still in her scrubs, comes in holding the hand of AMAHLE (8), who is wearing pyjamas under a yellow raincoat and has clearly been crying.
I'm sorry to come so late. We lost a giraffe.
A giraffe.
A toy one. His name is Gerald. He has a blue scarf and one of his legs is shorter than the others.
When did you last see Gerald?
On the escalator. I was holding him up so he could see the pigeons, and then he wasn't there any more.
shots.rationale: Captures the emotional introduction of Amahle's lost toy giraffe and Zanele's recording of the details.

shots.source:
Zanele writes it carefully in the ledger.
Giraffe. Gerald. Blue scarf. One short leg.
A knock on the open door. SAM (20s), a bicycle courier in a dripping rain cape, holds up a clipboard.
shots.rationale: Documents Zanele's note-taking and the arrival of the delivery courier Sam.

shots.source:
Delivery for a Mr. Dube? I was told to bring it here at eleven exactly.
Sam hands over a flat white box. Mr. Dube frowns at it.
I didn't order anything.
shots.rationale: Shows Mr. Dube's confusion upon receiving the unexpected package and Sam's request for a signature.

shots.source:
It's paid for. Sign here, please.
He signs. Sam salutes with the clipboard and is gone.
shots.rationale: Focuses on Mr. Dube's reaction as he signs the delivery receipt, emphasizing his surprise.

shots.source:
Tebogo finishes the tune and lowers the violin. The two officers stand in front of him.
Evening. That's a fine instrument.
shots.rationale: Establishes the violin's return and the officers' presence as Tebogo lowers the instrument.

shots.source:
It isn't mine.
Suspect admits instrument is not his.
Van Wyk.
shots.rationale: Captures Tebogo's admission and Van Wyk's note-taking on the ownership detail.

shots.source:
I found it on the nine-fifteen, under a seat. I was going to take it to Lost Property, but the office light was off when I passed, and then it started raining, and then --
I thought if I played it, whoever lost it might hear.
shots.rationale: Frames the emotional beat of Tebogo playing for a lost owner and Koos's observation.

shots.source:
He's been playing for an hour. Nobody came.
Somebody might have. Pack it up, son. We're going for a walk.
shots.rationale: Follows the characters as Officer Moloi orders them to leave the platform.

shots.source:
Priya stands at the concourse railing with Zanele. The sleeping commuter snores under his newspaper.
Faintly, from far away, violin music echoes off the marble. Then it stops.
shots.rationale: Establishes the two characters and the sleeping commuter before the sound draws attention.

shots.source:
Did you hear that?
Hear what?
That was my grandfather's tune. I would know it anywhere. Nobody else plays it.
shots.rationale: Priya's intense reaction to the personal memory requires intimacy.

shots.source: She is already running toward the platforms.
shots.rationale: Captures Priya's urgency and Zanele's plea as they move together.

shots.source: Priya, wait!
shots.rationale: Zanele's desperate stop is best seen in a medium frame to show her body language.

shots.source:
Officer Moloi steers Tebogo through the door, the violin case under his arm. Officer Van Wyk follows. Then Priya, out of breath. Then Zanele.
Everyone is suddenly in the small room at once. Marmalade leaves in disgust.
shots.rationale: Establishes the chaotic entry of all characters into the cramped office space.

shots.source:
That's it. That's my case.
We found the suspect playing it on platform nine.
I'm not a suspect. I'm a musician.
He says he found it on the nine-fifteen.
Priya opens the case. Inside the lid, a faded photograph of an old man holding the same violin.
shots.rationale: Captures the close examination of the violin case and the revelation of the photograph inside the lid.

shots.source:
It's here. It's all here.
She turns to Tebogo.
You played his tune. How do you know his tune?
I didn't. The music was folded in the case. I just read it.
shots.rationale: Focuses on the emotional exchange and the question of identity through the shared tune.

shots.source:
A long moment. Then Priya laughs, and cries a little, and laughs again.
Officers, I believe this is a case of lost property, and lost property is my department.
shots.rationale: Frames the transition from personal emotion to the formal handover of lost property.

shots.source:
Then we'll leave it with you, Mr. Dube.
But Sarge, the paperwork --
Van Wyk.
shots.rationale: Records the procedural closing of the case and the officers' reluctant compliance.

shots.source:
The officers leave. Amahle tugs at her mother's scrubs.
Mama, what about Gerald?
shots.rationale: Brings the scene to a close by addressing the lingering question about Gerald.

shots.source:
High above the concourse, among iron beams and pigeons, Koos climbs a tall wooden LADDER with a torch in his teeth.
He reaches into a nest of twigs and newspaper and pulls out a small toy GIRAFFE in a blue scarf.
shots.rationale: Establishes Koos's precarious position and his careful retrieval of the giraffe in the dim light.

shots.source: A pigeon glares at him.
shots.rationale: Focuses on the pigeon's glare to create a brief tension before Koos's line.

shots.source: Sorry, my friend. He's already got a home.
shots.rationale: Captures Koos's apologetic delivery of the line about the giraffe having a home.

shots.source:
Koos comes in with the giraffe held up high like a trophy.
Is anybody missing a Gerald?
Amahle shrieks and hugs the giraffe so hard his short leg sticks straight out.
shots.rationale: Establishes the entrance and the immediate emotional reaction to the giraffe's return.

shots.source:
Gerald! You went to see the pigeons without me!
Thank you. Thank you, all of you.
Mr. Dube unties the string on the white box. Inside is a cake, iced with the words HAPPY RETIREMENT MR. DUBE - FROM PLATFORM 9.
shots.rationale: Captures the reunion dialogue and the presentation of the retirement cake.

shots.source:
Who did this?
Lost property. Nobody claimed it.
Mr. Dube looks at the cake for a long moment. He takes out his handkerchief and blows his nose, loudly.
shots.rationale: Frames the detective's investigation and the revelation of the lost property origin.

shots.source:
Well. Someone find me a knife. And plates. And Tebogo, if you would play something that isn't sad.
Tebogo looks at Priya. She hands him the violin.
Just one song. Then I need it back. I have somewhere to be at eight.
shots.rationale: Focuses on the transaction of the violin and the request for a non-sad song.

shots.source: Tebogo plays something bright and quick. Amahle dances with Gerald. Koos taps his broom. Even Marmalade comes back to the doorway to watch.
shots.rationale: A tight shot on the cat's final reaction caps the scene's warmth.

shots.source:
The rain has stopped. Pale gold light slides along the rails. The first train of the day sighs to a stop.
Priya steps aboard with the violin case held tight against her chest. At the window she waves.
shots.rationale: Introduces Priya boarding and Mr. Dube's final watch wind as the train arrives.

shots.source: On the platform, Tebogo raises his hand. Beside him, Mr. Dube winds his pocket watch one last time and looks up at the station clock.
shots.rationale: Frames Tebogo's raised hand as a focused goodbye gesture.

shots.source: Right on time.
shots.rationale: Captures the goodbye gestures and Mr. Dube's line confirming the train's punctuality.

shots.source: The six-oh-five to Pretoria is now departing from platform four.
shots.rationale: Highlights the announcer's voice delivering the departure information.

shots.source: The train pulls away into the morning.
shots.rationale: Shows the train pulling away into the dawn sky.
